spans.s:
Iṣīkā, ‘a stalk of reed grass,’ occurs frequently from the
Atharvaveda^1 onwards, often as an emblem of fragility. In
the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka^2 it seems to denote the pin fixed in
the bar of a pen to keep cattle in (argaleṣīke, ‘bolt and pin’).
A basket (śūrpa) of Iṣīkā is referred to in the Śatapatha
Brāhmaṇa.^3
1) Av. vii. 56, 4; xii. 2, 54; Śatapatha
Brāhmaṇa, iv. 3, 4, 16, etc.; Jaiminīya
Brāhmaṇa, i. 9; ii. 134; Chāndogya
Upaniṣad, v. 24, 3; Kāṭhaka Upaniṣad,
ii. 6, 17, etc.; Nirukta, ix. 8.
2) ii. 16 (v. l. ˚ike).
3) i. 1, 4, 19.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 71;
Oertel, Journal of the American Oriental
Society, 19, 122, n. 3.
